Rix Asset Maintenance is seeking experienced Site Supervisors to join our team in NSW, supporting a number of slope stabilization projects across the civil, mining and infrastructure sectors throughout New South Wales.

Full time positions available with projects located across New South Wales.

About the Role

As the Site Supervisor, you will oversee all aspects of geotechnical stabilization works including various Drilling operations, Anchor installation, Grouting, Anchor testing, Rock fall netting and catch fence installation, Steel fixing, Formwork, Concrete, Shotcrete, and Scaling.

This role requires a strong leader who can lead and manage rope access construction teams while ensuring safety, productivity, and quality standards are consistently met.

Key Responsibilities

* Supervision and coordination of rope access crews including subcontractors, suppliers, plant and equipment
* Ensure that plant, equipment, staff and subcontractors operate within safe working conditions and ensure that all operations meet the environmental, safety and legislative requirements
* Conduct pre-starts, toolbox talks, and safety briefings
* Complete daily reports, safety documentation, and permit systems
* Conduct risk assessments, pre-work safety checks and equipment inspections while ensuring compliance is within industry standards
* Oversee installation of ground support systems including rock bolts, mesh, and shotcrete preparation
* Monitor work quality and productivity of rope access teams

Required Qualifications & Experience

* IRATA Rope Access Certification (preferred)
* White card
* Driving licence
* Minimum 3 years experience in ground engineering / civil infrastructure
* Demonstrated experience supervising rope access teams
* Experience in slope stabilization, scaling, rock bolting, or geotechnical works
* Previous mining site experience strongly preferred
* Strong knowledge of rope access safety procedures and risk management

Key Attributes

* Strong leadership and communication skills
* Safety-focused mindset

Job Title: Office Manager (Farsi/English Speaking)
Location: North Adelaide, SA
Salary/Remuneration: $78,000 AUD per annum + 11.5% Superannuation
Job Type: Full-time
Position Summary
The Office Manager is responsible for planning, organising and coordinating the administrative operations of Ghanbari & Associates Pty Ltd. The role ensures the efficient functioning of the office while supporting the firm's Iranian and Afghan client base through effective communication in both Farsi and English.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
•	Manage the day-to-day administrative operations of the office.
•	Develop, implement and maintain office systems, procedures and administrative processes.
•	Coordinate workflow and oversee administrative support activities to ensure efficient service delivery.
•	Manage client appointments, correspondence, records and document management systems.
•	Liaise with clients, government agencies and external service providers.
•	Assist Farsi-speaking clients by explaining processes, translating communications and facilitating effective client engagement.
•	Monitor office resources, supplies and equipment and arrange maintenance when required.
•	Support management with business administration, reporting and operational planning.
•	Assist with staff coordination, onboarding and training of administrative personnel.
•	Ensure compliance with office policies, privacy requirements and professional standards.
Skills and Experience
•	Relevant qualification and/or experience in office administration or management (Equivalent to ANZSCO Skill Level 2).
•	Demonstrated experience managing office operations and administrative systems.
•	Strong organisational, communication and client service skills.
•	Fluency in both Farsi (Persian) and English (Essential).
•	Ability to work with culturally diverse clients and maintain confidentiality.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and common business administration software.
Why Farsi is Required
A significant proportion of Ghanbari & Associates' clients are from Iranian and Afghan backgrounds and have limited English proficiency. Fluency in Farsi and English is essential to facilitate effective communication, explain legal and administrative processes, assist with documentation, and maintain a high standard of client service.
How to Apply
Please submit your resume and a cover letter detailing your language skills and experience directly through this portal or forward them to ADVISORY@IMMIGRATIONAUST.COM

Your new company  Join a Government organisation that supports services to a nationally significant workforce. This organisation is committed to delivering high-quality services, maintaining strong stakeholder relationships, and driving strategic communication outcomes across a diverse operational environment.   Your new role  
 As the Communication Manager, you'll act as the trusted communications adviser for a portfolio of business areas, partnering directly with senior executives to plan and deliver high-impact communication strategies and products. 
 Working across both internal and external communications, you'll take ownership of communication planning, executive messaging, issues management and digital content delivery. You'll be responsible for translating complex operational information into clear, engaging content and ensuring messaging is consistent across multiple channels and audiences. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Leading end-to-end communication strategies for major business initiatives and organisational priorities. 
 Providing high-level advice to senior executives on communication risks, opportunities and stakeholder engagement approaches. 
 Developing executive briefs, key messages, communication plans, web content, articles, speeches and organisational announcements. 
 Managing digital publishing and content governance processes, ensuring compliance with government accessibility and digital standards. 
 Monitoring communication performance and providing insights and recommendations to improve engagement outcomes. 
 Managing, leading and mentoring a small team. 
 
  What you'll need to succeed  
 
 Baseline security clearance is required. 
 Significant experience delivering strategic communications within government, corporate or highly regulated environments. 
 Demonstrated success developing communication plans, executive messaging and stakeholder engagement strategies for complex projects or organisational change initiatives. 
 Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to quickly distil technical or policy-heavy information into clear, audience-focused content. 
 Strong experience managing website content, digital publishing workflows and content governance processes. 
 The confidence to influence senior stakeholders and provide trusted communications advice in a fast-moving environment. 
 Experience balancing multiple priorities while managing competing deadlines and responding to emerging issues. 
 Familiarity with platforms such as GovCMS or similar enterprise content management systems will be highly regarded. 
 
  What you'll get in return  
 
 Attractive EL1-equivalent hourly rate.

 North Canberra-based opportunity with flexible working arrangements available in line with business requirements.

Location: 8 Moona Creek Road, Vincentia, NSW 2540
Employment type: Full-time (38 hours per week)


Qualifications Required:

Certificate III or higher qualification in Cookery or equivalent qualification.


Experience Required:

At least 3 years of relevant experience in cooking role is required. Experience gained as a Kitchen Hand or Restaurant Manager will not be considered as relevant cooking experience.

Applicants with experience in Japanese or Korean cuisine will be highly regarded.


Job Description:

The Cook will be responsible for preparing, cooking and presenting hot food menu items while ensuring food quality, food safety compliance and efficient kitchen operations. The Cook will also assist with the preparation of ingredients used by the sushi team and will work closely with the owner to monitor stock levels and order supplies.

Duties and Responsibilities:

The position’s duties include but not limited to:

- Prepare, cook and present a variety of hot food items in accordance with the business’ recipes and quality standards.
- Prepare ingredients by washing, cutting, marinating, seasoning and portioning food prior to service.
- Monitor cooking times and temperatures to ensure food is cooked consistently and safely.
- Ensure all meals are prepared and served promptly during busy service periods.
- Maintain food quality, presentation and portion control to ensure consistency across all menu items.
- Assist with planning daily food production based on customer demand and stock availability.
- Monitor stock levels and notify management when ingredients and kitchen supplies require replenishment.
- Receive, inspect and correctly store food deliveries in accordance with food safety requirements.
- Rotate stock using FIFO (First In, First Out) principles and minimise food wastage.
- Maintain a clean, organised and hygienic kitchen by cleaning workstations, equipment and food preparation areas throughout each shift.
- Ensure compliance with all food safety, sanitation and workplace health and safety regulations.
- Assist with the development of new menu items and suggest improvements to existing dishes where appropriate.
- Work collaboratively with other kitchen and front-of-house staff to ensure efficient service for both takeaway and seated customers.
- Report equipment faults, food quality issues or safety concerns to management promptly.
- Perform other kitchen-related duties as reasonably directed by management.
